ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari assigns the relative clause and conditional sentence as أرأيت's two objects, omits the first conditional answer in favor of the second, and treats the middle repeated أرأيت as emphatic.
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r13.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : ما متعلق { أرأيت } ؟ قلت : { الذي ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية ، وهما في موضع المفعولين

ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that parsing: the second object of أرأيت must be an interrogative clause, as in Qur'anic examples, rather than the relative plus conditional proposed by al-Zamakhshari.
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r14.anchor: وعندنا أن المفعول الثاني لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية ، كقوله : { أفرأيت الذي تولى وأعطى قليلاً وأكدى أعنده علم الغيب }

ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r15.claim: Abū Ḥayyān instead parses the first أرأيت with the relative as its first object; the later two instances have omitted objects recoverable from the servant or forbidding man and from the final interrogative clause.
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r15.anchor: ويجعل مفعول { أرأيت } الأولى هو الموصول ، وجاء بعده { أرأيت } ، وهي تطلب مفعولين ، وأرأيت الثانية كذلك

ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r16.claim: The successive omissions are not a case of syntactic competition, since clauses cannot be pronominally omitted; they are ordinary ellipses.
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r16.anchor: وهؤلاء الطوالب ليس طلبها على طريق التنازع ، لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها ، وإنما ذلك من باب الحذف في غير التنازع

ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r17.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhshari's allowance of an interrogative clause as a conditional answer without fa: grammarians require fa after a construction involving a request, except in poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN:96:10/r17.anchor: وأما تجويز الزمخشري وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء ، فلا أعلم أحداً أجازه ، بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء

ALUSI:96:9/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī introduces the prohibition of prayer as one manifestation of human tyranny and as the occasion for a warning.
ALUSI:96:9/r1.anchor: ذكر لبعض آثار الطغيان ووعيد عليها

ALUSI:96:9/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:96:9/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Abū Jahl vowed to trample the Prophet while he prayed; when he approached he recoiled, describing fire, terror, and wings, and the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb; the sūra’s end was revealed. No grading is stated.
ALUSI:96:9/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن أبا جهل حلف باللات والعزى لئن رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

ALUSI:96:9/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:96:9/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the preventer as Umayya b. Khalaf, who forbade Salmān to pray; al-Ālūsī says this is hardly sound because Salmān accepted Islam in Medina after the Hijra while the sūra is Meccan, though the verse’s general warning would include Umayya if the incident occurred.
ALUSI:96:9/r3.anchor: وقول الحسن هو أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة لا يكاد يصح

ALUSI:96:9/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:9/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the prayer was ẓuhr; another account says it was Islam’s first congregational prayer, with the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿAlī, and that Abū Ṭālib urged Jaʿfar to join his cousin and left happily, composing verses in their support.
ALUSI:96:9/r4.anchor: على ما حكى أبو حيان صلاة الظهر وحكي أيضاً أنها كانت تصلي جماعة وهي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام

ALUSI:96:9/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r5.claim: Prayer was obligatory on the Miʿrāj, usually dated one year before Hijra (Ibn Ḥazm says consensus; Ibn Fāris says 1y3m, al-Suddī 1y5m); Abū Ṭālib died about three years before Hijra, before Khadīja by three or five days, while she died ten years after the mission.
ALUSI:96:9/r5.anchor: الصلاة فرضت ليلة الإسراء بلا خلاف وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة

ALUSI:96:9/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r6.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI:96:9/r6.claim: Al-Zuhrī’s reported dating places the Miʿrāj five years after the beginning of the mission; Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmits it, and al-Nawawī and al-Qurṭubī prefer it, though al-Ālūsī notes objections to that chronology.
ALUSI:96:9/r6.anchor: حكى القاضي عياض عن الزهري ورجحه النووي والقرطبي أن الإسراء كان بعد البعث بخمس سنين لكن قيل عليه ما قيل

ALUSI:96:9/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:9/r7.claim: Some take yanha as ‘prevents’; al-Ālūsī says this wording suggests Abū Jahl could only attempt to prevent the prayer, not do more.
ALUSI:96:9/r7.anchor: والنهي قيل بمعنى المنع وعبر به إشارة إلى عدم اقتدار اللعين على غير ذلك

ALUSI:96:9/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:96:9/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl verbally challenged the Prophet while he prayed, asking whether he had not forbidden him; al-Tirmidhī authenticates this report.
ALUSI:96:9/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

ALUSI:96:9/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r9.claim: The imperfect verb evokes the past scene as if it were happening now, lending vividness to its strange character.
ALUSI:96:9/r9.anchor: والتعبير بما يفيد الاستقبال لاستحضار الصورة الماضية لنوع غرابة

ALUSI:96:9/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:9/r10.claim: On one analysis, raʾayta is cognitive, as in 96:13: the first object is the relative clause’s referent, while later objects are elided or resumed by a pronoun or demonstrative; the third question’s second object is ‘Does he not know that God sees?’
ALUSI:96:9/r10.anchor: الرؤية قيل قلبية وكذا في قوله تعالى

ALUSI:96:9/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r11.claim: The example with repeated akhbirnī is not syntactic tanāzuʿ: clauses cannot be elided as such, and the construction instead involves semantic demand and deletion outside tanāzuʿ.
ALUSI:96:9/r11.anchor: وليس ذلك من التنازع لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها وإنما هو من الطلب المعنوي

ALUSI:96:9/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r12.claim: The conditional clauses’ apodoses are omitted because ‘Does he not know?’ indicates them; another analysis lets raʾayta itself anticipate the subsequently stated matter.
ALUSI:96:9/r12.anchor: وجواب الشرط في الجملتين محذوف لدلالة ألم يعلم عليه ويقدر حسبما تقتضيه الصناعة

ALUSI:96:9/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r13.claim: The concealed subjects of kāna and the verbs following it refer to the person forbidding prayer.
ALUSI:96:9/r13.anchor: والضمائر المستترة في { كان } وما بعد

ALUSI:96:9/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r14.claim: Raʾayta means ‘tell me’: because seeing leads to knowing, asking whether one has seen stands for asking about what was seen.
ALUSI:96:9/r14.anchor: والمراد من أرأيت أخبرني فإن الرؤية لما كانت سبباً للعلم أجري الاستفهام عنها مجرى الاستخبار عن متعلقها

ALUSI:96:9/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r15.claim: This use of raʾayta as inquiry is said to work with either visual or cognitive seeing; grammarians have two positions on the construction.
ALUSI:96:9/r15.anchor: وهذا الإجراء على ما يفهم من كلام بعض الأئمة يكون مع الرؤية البصرية والرؤية القلبية وللنحاة فيه قولان

ALUSI:96:9/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r16.claim: One reading takes the tanwīn on ʿabdan as indefiniteness and the time phrase as indicating that the prohibition occurs while the person is praying.
ALUSI:96:9/r16.anchor: وتنوين { عبداً } على ما هو ظاهر كلام البعض

ALUSI:96:9/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r17.claim: The clauses are separated so each denunciation and threat stands on its own, heightening the censure and warning.
ALUSI:96:9/r17.anchor: وفصل بين الجمل للاعتناء بأمر التشنيع والوعيد حيث أشعر أن كل جملة مقصودة على حيالها

ALUSI:96:9/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r18.claim: Al-Ālūsī reads a three-stage escalation: the first threat censures the prohibition without specifying the preventer’s state, the next addresses his claimed righteousness, and the last his actual denial and turning away.
ALUSI:96:9/r18.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي ثم شنع وأوعد جل وعلا عليه مع التعرض لحاله الزعمي

ALUSI:96:9/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r19.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:9/r19.claim: The majority do not restrict the two conditional descriptions as al-Ālūsī’s staged analysis does: they contrast claimed right guidance or piety with the preventer’s actual denial and turning away.
ALUSI:96:9/r19.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا حيث قالوا إن كان على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه

ALUSI:96:9/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r20.claim: One explanation makes both conditions lead to the same point: the first feigns latitude before mocking the notion that forbidding worship and urging idols could be guidance; the second mockingly grants a condition everyone knows is false.
ALUSI:96:9/r20.anchor: وذكر أن الشرط الثاني تكرار للأول لأن معنى الأول أنه ليس على الهدى وأوضح بأن إدخال حرف الشرط في الأول لإرخاء العنان صورة والتهكم حقيقة

ALUSI:96:9/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r21.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:9/r21.claim: Another parse makes raʾayta in the first question visual and in the second and third cognitive; the final question’s answer is explicit, while the prior conditional points forward to it.
ALUSI:96:9/r21.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان وفي الثانية والثالثة قلبية

ALUSI:96:9/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r22.claim: On that parse, leaving the last question uncoordinated marks it as independently actual and makes its answer an ensuing threat; the earlier conditions merely widen the scope.
ALUSI:96:9/r22.anchor: ولم تعطف الأخيرة على ما قبلها للإيذان باستقلالها بالوقوع في نفس الأمر وباستتباع الوعيد

ALUSI:96:9/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r23.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:9/r23.claim: A further analysis treats all three questions as cognitive and the second as a repetition of the first; both conditions fill its second-object slot, with the final answer explicit and the first answer elided.
ALUSI:96:9/r23.anchor: وقيل أرأيت في الجملتين الثانية والثالثة تكرار للأولى والشرطيتان بجوابهما سادتان مسد المفعول الثاني للأولى

ALUSI:96:9/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r24.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:96:9/r24.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī permits an interrogative conditional apodosis without faʾ and cites 6:47; al-Raḍī accepts this, but Abū Ḥayyān and al-Damāmīnī object that an interrogative requires faʾ, absent here.
ALUSI:96:9/r24.anchor: الزمخشري في كشافه وارتضاه الرضي واستشهد له

ALUSI:96:9/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r25.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:9/r25.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says he knows no one who allows an interrogative sentence to answer a condition without faʾ; al-Damāmīnī likewise finds it problematic to parse ‘Will anyone perish?’ as the apodosis without the required faʾ.
ALUSI:96:9/r25.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إن وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء لا أعلم أحد أجازه بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء

ALUSI:96:9/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r26.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:9/r26.claim: Abū Ḥayyān and others object that raʾayta’s second object must be an interrogative or oath clause, not a conditional; al-Khafājī answers that the conditional and its interrogative answer can occupy that slot, as al-Raḍī and al-Damāmīnī allow, consistent with Sibawayh’s preferred view.
ALUSI:96:9/r26.anchor: واعترض أيضاً جعل الجملة الشرطية في موضع المفعول الثاني

ALUSI:96:9/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r27.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r27.claim: The addressee is left outside both the preventer and the worshipper because the context calls for an observer distinct from them.
ALUSI:96:9/r27.anchor: ولم يجعلوا فيما ذكر الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا للكافر الناهي لأن السياق مقتض لخروج الناهي والمنهي عن مورد الخطاب

ALUSI:96:9/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r28.speaker: جمع
ALUSI:96:9/r28.claim: A group takes the address throughout as directed to anyone capable of understanding; another view makes it address ‘the human,’ as in 96:8.
ALUSI:96:9/r28.anchor: والخطاب في الكل على ما اختاره جمع لكل من يصلح

ALUSI:96:9/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r29.speaker: البحر
ALUSI:96:9/r29.claim: Al-Baḥr prefers the Prophet as the addressee; another view allows the unbelieving preventer, while other proposals assign the questions to the Prophet or to anyone fit to understand.
ALUSI:96:9/r29.anchor: جعله للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجوز غيره جعله للكافر

ALUSI:96:9/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r30.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r30.claim: Another explanation takes the tanwīn on ‘a servant’ to magnify the Prophet, heighten the enormity of the prohibition, and intensify the wonder it provokes.
ALUSI:96:9/r30.anchor: والتنوين في عبداً لتفخيمه عليه الصلاة والسلام واستعظام النهي وتأكيد التعجيب منه

ALUSI:96:9/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r31.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:96:9/r31.claim: The Imam reads the second question as asking whether guidance and commanding piety would not better suit this rational, wealthy man than disbelief and opposition to God; it laments his loss of high rank for a base one.
ALUSI:96:9/r31.anchor: أرأيت إن صار على الهدى واشتغل بأمر نفسه أما كان يليق به ذلك إذ هو رجل عاقل ذو ثروة

ALUSI:96:9/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r32.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:9/r32.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn sees the first question as exposing the tyranny of a self-satisfied person who goes beyond ingratitude to urge disbelief; the next questions rebuke lost guidance and piety, then earned punishment and distance from God.
ALUSI:96:9/r32.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع

ALUSI:96:9/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r33.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r33.claim: Al-Ālūsī presents the preceding readings for reflection and leaves God’s intended meaning ultimately known to Him.
ALUSI:96:9/r33.anchor: وهو كما ترى فتأمل جميع ما تقدم والله تعالى بمراده أعلم

ALUSI:96:9/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r34.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r34.claim: The second question mentions commanding piety because forbidding something commands its opposite or entails that command; its mention there may supply what was omitted from the first question.
ALUSI:96:9/r34.anchor: لأن النهي عن الشيء أمر بضده أو مستلزم له

ALUSI:96:9/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r35.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r35.claim: One explanation says the first question omits the command to piety, included in the second, because prayer is practical worship and a stronger example of calling others than verbal instruction.
ALUSI:96:9/r35.anchor: واقتصر على ذكر الصلاة ولم يعكس لأن الأمر بالتقوى دعوة قولية والصلاة دعوة فعلية والفعل أقوى من القول

ALUSI:96:9/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r36.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:9/r36.claim: Another view says the first phrase describes forbidding someone while he is praying, not necessarily forbidding prayer itself; the prohibition could concern prayer or another matter.
ALUSI:96:9/r36.anchor: وقيل المذكور أولاً ليس النهي عن الصلاة بل النهي حين الصلاة وهو محتمل أن يكون لها أو لغيرها

ALUSI:96:9/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r37.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r37.claim: Although revealed about Abū Jahl, the threat applies to anyone who prevents prayer; it does not forbid objections to prayer in usurped property or disliked times, since the objection targets an accompanying quality rather than prayer itself.
ALUSI:96:9/r37.anchor: الآية وإن نزلت في أبي جهل عليه اللعنة لكن كل من نهى عن الصلاة ومنع منها فهو شريكه في الوعيد

ALUSI:96:9/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r38.speaker: علي
ALUSI:96:9/r38.claim: A report says ʿAlī saw people praying before the Eid prayer and said he had not seen the Prophet do that; asked why he did not stop them, he feared the verse’s threat. Another version says he preferred to relate the Prophet’s practice rather than forbid a worshipper.
ALUSI:96:9/r38.anchor: فروي عن أمير المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه رأى في المصلي أقواماً يصلون قبل صلاة العيد

ALUSI:96:9/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r39.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI:96:9/r39.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa similarly avoids direct prohibition: when Abū Yūsuf asks what a worshipper should say after rising from bowing, he gives the preferred phrase and instruction to prostrate without explicitly forbidding the alternative.
ALUSI:96:9/r39.anchor: وقد سلك نحو هذا المسلك أبو حنيفة عليه الرحمة فقد روي أن أبا يوسف قال له أيقول المصلي

ALUSI:96:9/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:9/r40.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:9/r40.claim: The caution about forbidding prayer extends to forbidding other forms of worship; verbal commands and circumstantial interference alike count, including distracting someone from worship, a common failing.
ALUSI:96:9/r40.anchor: ويقاس على النهي عن الصلاة النهي عن غيرها من أنواع العبادة ولا فرق بين النهي القالي والنهي الحالي

ALUSI:96:10/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r31.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r31.claim: The clauses are separated to intensify rebuke and warning and show that each has an independent point.
ALUSI:96:10/r31.anchor: وفصل بين الجمل للاعتناء بأمر التشنيع والوعيد حيث أشعر أن كل جملة مقصودة على حيالها

ALUSI:96:10/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r32.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r32.claim: First the passage warns generally against forbidding prayer: does the prohibiter not know God sees and will punish him?
ALUSI:96:10/r32.anchor: فشنع سبحانه على الناهي أولاً بنهيه عن الصلاة وأوعد عليه مطلقاً

ALUSI:96:10/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r35.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r35.claim: The sequence rises in severity: a general warning, one framed around the prohibiter’s claimed position, then one about his actual position.
ALUSI:96:10/r35.anchor: وهذا كالترقي في التشنيع والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا

ALUSI:96:10/r54.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r54.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:10/r54.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9–10 as exposing tyranny when a person feels self-sufficient, 96:11–12 as rebuking lost guidance and piety, and 96:13–14 as rebuking earned punishment and distance from God.
ALUSI:96:10/r54.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:10/r55.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r55.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r55.claim: Al-Ālūsī distances himself from ʿIṣām al-Dīn’s elaboration, inviting reflection and leaving the matter to God’s intended meaning.
ALUSI:96:10/r55.anchor: وهو كما ترى فتأمل جميع ما تقدم والله تعالى بمراده أعلم

ALUSI:96:11/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:96:11/r1.claim: Aḥmad, Muslim, al-Nasāʾī and others report from Abū Hurayra that Abū Jahl threatened the praying Prophet, recoiled at a trench of fire, terror and wings, and heard that angels would seize him; the sūra was then revealed from 96:6 to its end.
ALUSI:96:11/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن أبا جهل حلف باللات والعزى لئن رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

ALUSI:96:11/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI:96:11/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the commentators agree that the servant being stopped from prayer is the Messenger and the forbidding man is Abū Jahl.
ALUSI:96:11/r2.anchor: كما قال ابن عطية في أن العبد المصلي هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والناهي هو اللعين أبو جهل

ALUSI:96:11/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:96:11/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the forbidding man as Umayya b. Khalaf, who stopped Salmān from praying; al-Ālūsī says this is hardly sound because Salmān embraced Islam in Medina while the sūra is Meccan.
ALUSI:96:11/r3.anchor: وقول الحسن هو أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة لا يكاد يصح لأنه لا خلاف

ALUSI:96:11/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:11/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān relates that the prayer in question was the noon prayer.

ALUSI:96:11/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:11/r5.claim: A further account calls it the first congregational prayer in Islam: the Prophet prayed with Abū Bakr and ʿAlī; Abū Ṭālib passed with Jaʿfar, urged him to join his cousin, and left pleased.
ALUSI:96:11/r5.anchor: وحكي أيضاً أنها كانت تصلي جماعة وهي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام وأنه كان معه عليه الصلاة والسلام أبو بكر وعلي

ALUSI:96:11/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r6.speaker: أبو طالب
ALUSI:96:11/r6.claim: The cited poem attributed to Abū Ṭālib calls ʿAlī and Jaʿfar trusted kin in hardship and urges them not to abandon the Prophet but to support their maternal and paternal cousin.
ALUSI:96:11/r6.anchor: وأنشأ يقول : إن علياً وجعفراً ثقتي *** عند ملم الزمال والكرب

ALUSI:96:11/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī questions the Abū Ṭālib account: prayer was prescribed on the Night Journey, usually dated a year before the Hijra, whereas Abū Ṭālib died about three years before it. Reports place the Journey five years after the mission, a chronology criticized by others.
ALUSI:96:11/r7.anchor: وفي هذا نظر لأن الصلاة فرضت ليلة الإسراء بلا خلاف وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة

ALUSI:96:11/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r8.speaker: ابن حزم
ALUSI:96:11/r8.claim: Ibn Ḥazm claims consensus that the Night Journey was one year before the Hijra; Ibn Fāris gives one year and three months, and al-Suddī one year and five months.
ALUSI:96:11/r8.anchor: وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة وجزم ابن فارس بأنه كان قبلها بسنة وثلاثة أشهر وقال السدي

ALUSI:96:11/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r9.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI:96:11/r9.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reports al-Zuhrī's view that the Night Journey occurred five years after the prophetic mission; al-Nawawī and al-Qurṭubī favor it, though al-Ālūsī notes objections to that dating.
ALUSI:96:11/r9.anchor: حكى القاضي عياض عن الزهري ورجحه النووي والقرطبي أن الإسراء كان بعد البعث بخمس سنين لكن قيل عليه ما قيل

ALUSI:96:11/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī says nahy means forbidding; its wording suggests Abū Jahl could do no more than that, though some reports indicate he also verbally forbade the Prophet.
ALUSI:96:11/r10.anchor: والنهي قيل بمعنى المنع وعبر به إشارة إلى عدم اقتدار اللعين على غير ذلك

ALUSI:96:11/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:96:11/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl verbally told the Prophet, as he prayed, that he had forbidden him to do so; al-Tirmidhī authenticated this report.
ALUSI:96:11/r11.anchor: فقد أخرج أحمد والترمذي وصححه وغيرهما عن ابن عباس قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل

ALUSI:96:11/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r32.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:11/r32.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as evidence of the tyrant's arrogance when self-sufficient, 96:11 as reproach for losing the benefit of guidance and piety, 96:13 as reproach for earning punishment, and ألم يعلم as a severe threat.
ALUSI:96:11/r32.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:11/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r33.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r33.claim: Although revealed about Abū Jahl, the warning applies to everyone who stops prayer. It does not forbid objecting to prayer in usurped places or disliked times, since the objection concerns an accompanying attribute rather than prayer itself.
ALUSI:96:11/r33.anchor: ثم إن الآية وإن نزلت في أبي جهل عليه اللعنة لكن كل من نهى عن الصلاة ومنع منها فهو شريكه في الوعيد

ALUSI:96:11/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r34.speaker: علي
ALUSI:96:11/r34.claim: A report says ʿAlī saw people praying before the ʿĪd prayer; when asked why he did not forbid them, he feared the warning in this verse. Another version says he preferred to tell them what he had seen the Prophet do rather than forbid a worshipper.
ALUSI:96:11/r34.anchor: فروي عن أمير المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه رأى في المصلي أقواماً يصلون قبل صلاة العيد

ALUSI:96:11/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r35.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI:96:11/r35.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Abū Ḥanīfa likewise avoided a direct prohibition: asked by Abū Yūsuf about a prayer formula while rising from bowing, he stated the formula he favored and continued to prostration without explicitly forbidding it.
ALUSI:96:11/r35.anchor: وقد سلك نحو هذا المسلك أبو حنيفة عليه الرحمة فقد روي أن أبا يوسف قال له أيقول المصلي حين يرفع رأسه

ALUSI:96:11/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r36.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r36.claim: The warning extends by analogy to forbidding other worship, whether by words or conduct; distracting someone from worship also counts as a practical prohibition, a widespread affliction.
ALUSI:96:11/r36.anchor: ويقاس على النهي عن الصلاة النهي عن غيرها من أنواع العبادة ولا فرق بين النهي القالي والنهي الحالي

ALUSI:96:12/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI:96:12/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the commentators agree that the worshipper is the Messenger and the person forbidding him is Abu Jahl.
ALUSI:96:12/r1.anchor: كما قال ابن عطية في أن العبد المصلي هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والناهي هو اللعين أبو جهل

ALUSI:96:12/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:96:12/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl swore to trample the Prophet if he prayed; when he approached, he recoiled, describing fire and terror between them. The Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb, and 96:6 through the sūra’s end was revealed.
ALUSI:96:12/r2.anchor: أخرج أحمد ومسلم والنسائي وغيرهم عن أبي هريرة أن أبا جهل حلف باللات والعزى لئن رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

ALUSI:96:12/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:96:12/r3.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the forbidding person as Umayya b. Khalaf, who stopped Salman from praying.
ALUSI:96:12/r3.anchor: وقول الحسن هو أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة

ALUSI:96:12/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the report about Umayya and Salman scarcely holds: Salman became Muslim in Medina after the Hijra, whereas this sūra is Meccan.
ALUSI:96:12/r4.anchor: لا يكاد يصح لأنه لا خلاف في أن إسلام سلمان رضي الله تعالى عنه كان بالمدينة بعد الهجرة

ALUSI:96:12/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r5.claim: Although revealed about Abu Jahl, the warning applies to anyone who prevents prayer; the Umayya report, if true, falls under that general rule.
ALUSI:96:12/r5.anchor: نعم حكم الآية عام فإن كان ما حكي عن أمية واقعاً فحكمها شامل له

ALUSI:96:12/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:12/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the prayer in the incident was the noon prayer.
ALUSI:96:12/r6.anchor: كانت على ما حكى أبو حيان صلاة الظهر

ALUSI:96:12/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r7.claim: Another account says the prayer was congregational, the first congregation in Islam, with the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and ʿAlī present.
ALUSI:96:12/r7.anchor: وحكي أيضاً أنها كانت تصلي جماعة وهي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام وأنه كان معه عليه الصلاة والسلام أبو بكر وعلي

ALUSI:96:12/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r8.claim: The account says Abū Ṭālib passed with Jaʿfar, told him to join his cousin in prayer, and left delighted; he recited a poem affirming that ʿAlī and Jaʿfar would support the Prophet.
ALUSI:96:12/r8.anchor: فمر أبو طالب ومعه ابنه جعفر فقال له يا بني صل جناح ابن عمك وانصرف مسروراً

ALUSI:96:12/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r9.speaker: ابن حزم
ALUSI:96:12/r9.claim: Ibn Ḥazm claims consensus that prayer was imposed one year before Hijra; Ibn Fāris gives one year and three months, and al-Suddī one year and five months.
ALUSI:96:12/r9.anchor: وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة وجزم ابن فارس بأنه كان قبلها بسنة وثلاثة أشهر وقال السدي بسنة وخمسة أشهر

ALUSI:96:12/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that Abū Ṭālib died about three years before Hijra, shortly before Khadīja, so on the usual chronology he could not have witnessed obligatory prayer.
ALUSI:96:12/r10.anchor: فأبو طالب على هذا لم يدرك فرضية الصلاة نعم حكى القاضي عياض

ALUSI:96:12/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r11.speaker: القاضي عياض
ALUSI:96:12/r11.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmits from al-Zuhrī that the Night Journey occurred five years after the mission began, a dating endorsed by al-Nawawī and al-Qurṭubī; al-Ālūsī notes objections to it.
ALUSI:96:12/r11.anchor: حكى القاضي عياض عن الزهري ورجحه النووي والقرطبي أن الإسراء كان بعد البعث بخمس سنين لكن قيل عليه ما قيل

ALUSI:96:12/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r12.claim: Some understand the prohibition as prevention; its wording hints that Abu Jahl lacked the power to do more than forbid.
ALUSI:96:12/r12.anchor: والنهي قيل بمعنى المنع وعبر به إشارة إلى عدم اقتدار اللعين على غير ذلك

ALUSI:96:12/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:96:12/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports an explicit verbal prohibition while the Prophet prayed; al-Tirmidhī authenticated the report.
ALUSI:96:12/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل فقال ألم أنهك عن هذا

ALUSI:96:12/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r14.claim: The present or future form evokes the past scene vividly because the incident is strange.
ALUSI:96:12/r14.anchor: والتعبير بما يفيد الاستقبال لاستحضار الصورة الماضية لنوع غرابة

ALUSI:96:12/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r15.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r15.claim: Some take the vision in the first and third questions as intellectual rather than visual; grammarians hold two views on this construction.
ALUSI:96:12/r15.anchor: والرؤية قيل قلبية وكذا في قوله تعالى : { أَرَءيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وتولى }

ALUSI:96:12/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r16.claim: Here arayta means Tell me: because seeing leads to knowledge, the question functions as an inquiry into what is seen.
ALUSI:96:12/r16.anchor: والمراد من أرأيت أخبرني فإن الرؤية لما كانت سبباً للعلم أجري الاستفهام عنها مجرى الاستخبار عن متعلقها

ALUSI:96:12/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r17.claim: In one parsing, the first question’s object is the relative clause, while those of the second and third are omitted pronouns or demonstratives; the third question’s second object is ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى.
ALUSI:96:12/r17.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه أو اسم إشارة يشار به إليه

ALUSI:96:12/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r19.speaker: بعض الأئمة
ALUSI:96:12/r19.claim: Some authorities say the question construction works with both visual and intellectual seeing; grammarians differ over its analysis.
ALUSI:96:12/r19.anchor: هذا الإجراء على ما يفهم من كلام بعض الأئمة يكون مع الرؤية البصرية والرؤية القلبية وللنحاة فيه قولان

ALUSI:96:12/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r20.speaker: جمع
ALUSI:96:12/r20.claim: A group takes the address throughout as directed to anyone capable of understanding; another view makes it a generic address to humankind, as in 96:8.
ALUSI:96:12/r20.anchor: والخطاب في الكل على ما اختاره جمع لكل من يصلح أن يكون مخاطباً ممن له مسكة

ALUSI:96:12/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r21.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:96:12/r21.claim: Some take the indefinite form of ʿabdan as simple indefiniteness; another analysis uses it to magnify the Prophet and intensify the astonishment.
ALUSI:96:12/r21.anchor: وتنوين { عبداً } على ما هو ظاهر كلام البعض للتنكير

ALUSI:96:12/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r22.claim: Restricting the prohibition to the time clause suggests it occurred during prayer; separating the clauses gives each reproach and threat independent force.
ALUSI:96:12/r22.anchor: وتقييد النهي بالظرف يشعر بأن النهي عن الصلاة حال التلبس بها وفصل بين الجمل للاعتناء بأمر التشنيع والوعيد

ALUSI:96:12/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r23.claim: Al-Ālūsī reads three escalating reproaches: first for forbidding prayer without regard to the forbidder’s state, then on the state he claims, and finally on his actual denial and turning away, each ending in divine threat.
ALUSI:96:12/r23.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي ثم شنع وأوعد جل وعلا عليه مع التعرض لحاله الزعمي

ALUSI:96:12/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r33.speaker: البحر
ALUSI:96:12/r33.claim: Earlier interpreters do not address the Prophet or the unbelieving forbidder, since context removes both from the address; al-Baḥr favors the Prophet, while another view permits addressing the unbeliever.
ALUSI:96:12/r33.anchor: ولم يجعلوا فيما ذكر الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا للكافر الناهي لأن السياق مقتض لخروج الناهي والمنهي عن مورد الخطاب

ALUSI:96:12/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r37.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r37.claim: Another explanation says the first prohibition occurred during prayer but could concern prayer or something else; prayer perfects the worshipper and guides others, so forbidding during it could block both, hence the later mention of piety.
ALUSI:96:12/r37.anchor: وقيل المذكور أولاً ليس النهي عن الصلاة بل النهي حين الصلاة وهو محتمل أن يكون لها أو لغيرها

ALUSI:96:12/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r39.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:12/r39.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as exposing tyranny born of self-sufficiency, 96:11 as reproaching lost guidance and piety, 96:13 as reproaching earned punishment and distance from God, and 96:14 as the threat after both reproaches.
ALUSI:96:12/r39.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:12/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r40.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r40.claim: The warning does not prohibit advising against prayer in a usurped place or at a disliked time, because the objection concerns an accompanying attribute rather than prayer itself.
ALUSI:96:12/r40.anchor: ولا يلزم على ذلك المنع عن النهي عن الصلاة في الدار المغصوبة والأوقات المكروهة لأن المنهي عنه في الحقيقة ليس عن الصلاة نفسها

ALUSI:96:12/r41.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r41.speaker: علي
ALUSI:96:12/r41.claim: ʿAlī saw people praying before Eid and said he had not seen the Messenger do so; when asked why he did not forbid them, he feared falling under this warning. Another version says he preferred to tell them the prophetic practice.
ALUSI:96:12/r41.anchor: فروي عن أمير المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه رأى في المصلي أقواماً يصلون قبل صلاة العيد فقال ما رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يفعل ذلك

ALUSI:96:12/r42.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r42.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI:96:12/r42.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa likewise avoided explicit prohibition: when Abū Yūsuf asked about saying Allah forgive me on rising from bowing, he instructed him to say ربنا لك الحمد and prostrate.
ALUSI:96:12/r42.anchor: وقد سلك نحو هذا المسلك أبو حنيفة عليه الرحمة فقد روي أن أبا يوسف قال له أيقول المصلي حين يرفع رأسه من الركوع

ALUSI:96:12/r43.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r43.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r43.claim: The warning extends by analogy to forbidding other forms of worship; verbal and practical obstruction are alike, including distracting someone from worship.
ALUSI:96:12/r43.anchor: ويقاس على النهي عن الصلاة النهي عن غيرها من أنواع العبادة ولا فرق بين النهي القالي والنهي الحالي ومنه أن يشغل المرء المرء عن ذلك

ALUSI:96:13/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r1.claim: The passage from 96:9 onward recounts some consequences of human tyranny and threatens the one who prevents prayer.
ALUSI:96:13/r1.anchor: ذكر لبعض آثار الطغيان ووعيد عليها

ALUSI:96:13/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:96:13/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Abū Jahl swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā to trample the Prophet, then retreated from a fiery trench, terror, and wings; the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb. This occasioned 96:6 through the sūra’s end.
ALUSI:96:13/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن أبا جهل حلف باللات والعزى

ALUSI:96:13/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:96:13/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the prohibitor as Umayya b. Khalaf and the worshipper as Salmān; al-Ālūsī says this report is unsound because Salmān became Muslim in Medina while the sūra is Meccan.
ALUSI:96:13/r3.anchor: وقول الحسن هو أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة لا يكاد يصح

ALUSI:96:13/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r4.claim: The sūra is Meccan and Salmān became Muslim after the Hijra; if Umayya’s reported action occurred, the verse’s general threat would include him.
ALUSI:96:13/r4.anchor: فإن كان ما حكي عن أمية واقعاً فحكمها شامل له

ALUSI:96:13/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:13/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reports that the prayer referred to was the noon prayer.
ALUSI:96:13/r5.anchor: على ما حكى أبو حيان صلاة الظهر

ALUSI:96:13/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r6.claim: Another account says this was a congregational prayer, the first congregation in Islam, with Abū Bakr and ʿAlī; Abū Ṭālib passed with Jaʿfar and urged him to join his cousin.
ALUSI:96:13/r6.anchor: وحكي أيضاً أنها كانت تصلي جماعة وهي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام

ALUSI:96:13/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r7.speaker: أبو طالب
ALUSI:96:13/r7.claim: Abū Ṭālib’s cited poem calls ʿAlī and Jaʿfar his trusted support in hardship, says kin will not abandon the Prophet, and urges them to defend their cousin.

ALUSI:96:13/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r8.claim: Prayer was instituted on the night of the Isrāʾ by consensus; Ibn Ḥazm specifically claims consensus that this was one year before the Hijra.
ALUSI:96:13/r8.anchor: وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة

ALUSI:96:13/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r9.speaker: ابن فارس
ALUSI:96:13/r9.claim: Ibn Fāris dates the Isrāʾ to one year and three months before the Hijra.
ALUSI:96:13/r9.anchor: وجزم ابن فارس بأنه كان قبلها بسنة وثلاثة أشهر

ALUSI:96:13/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r10.speaker: السدي
ALUSI:96:13/r10.claim: Al-Suddī dates the Isrāʾ to one year and five months before the Hijra.

ALUSI:96:13/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r11.claim: The congregational-prayer account involving Abū Ṭālib conflicts with the chronology: he died about three years before the Hijra, before prayer was prescribed.
ALUSI:96:13/r11.anchor: وموت أبي طالب كان قبل الهجرة بنحو ثلاث سنين

ALUSI:96:13/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r12.speaker: القاضي عياض
ALUSI:96:13/r12.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmits al-Zuhrī’s view, preferred by al-Nawawī and al-Qurṭubī, that the Isrāʾ occurred five years after the prophetic commission; al-Ālūsī notes objections to it.
ALUSI:96:13/r12.anchor: حكى القاضي عياض عن الزهري ورجحه النووي والقرطبي أن الإسراء كان بعد البعث بخمس سنين

ALUSI:96:13/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r13.claim: The word for forbidding is explained as preventing; its use hints that the tyrant could do no more than this, though other reports show verbal prohibition.
ALUSI:96:13/r13.anchor: والنهي قيل بمعنى المنع وعبر به إشارة إلى عدم اقتدار اللعين على غير ذلك

ALUSI:96:13/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:96:13/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl came while the Prophet prayed and repeatedly challenged him, “Did I not forbid you?” Al-Tirmidhī authenticated this report.
ALUSI:96:13/r14.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

ALUSI:96:13/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r17.claim: In the principal parse, the first raʾayta takes the relative clause as its first object; the second and third have an omitted first object referring back, and the third’s second object is “does he not know that God sees?”
ALUSI:96:13/r17.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه

ALUSI:96:13/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r18.claim: The apparent ellipsis here is semantic request, not tanāzuʿ: clauses cannot be elided as competing syntactic governors; al-Ālūsī illustrates with a report about Zayd.
ALUSI:96:13/r18.anchor: وليس ذلك من التنازع لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها وإنما هو من الطلب المعنوي

ALUSI:96:13/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r20.claim: The address in all three questions may be to anyone capable of understanding; another view takes it as addressing humankind, as in “to your Lord” at 96:8.
ALUSI:96:13/r20.anchor: والخطاب في الكل على ما اختاره جمع لكل من يصلح أن يكون مخاطباً

ALUSI:96:13/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r21.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r21.claim: Some take the indefinite accusative ʿabdan at face value as indefiniteness.
ALUSI:96:13/r21.anchor: وتنوين { عبداً } على ما هو ظاهر كلام البعض للتنكير

ALUSI:96:13/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r22.claim: Al-Ālūsī also prefers reading the indefinite as magnifying the Prophet, the audacity of the prohibition, and the astonishment it deserves.
ALUSI:96:13/r22.anchor: والتنوين في عبداً لتفخيمه عليه الصلاة والسلام واستعظام النهي وتأكيد التعجيب منه

ALUSI:96:13/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r23.claim: Restricting the prohibition with the temporal clause suggests that the prohibition occurred while the person was engaged in prayer.
ALUSI:96:13/r23.anchor: وتقييد النهي بالظرف يشعر بأن النهي عن الصلاة حال التلبس بها

ALUSI:96:13/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r24.claim: The clauses are separated to intensify censure and threat, presenting each as independently deserving condemnation.
ALUSI:96:13/r24.anchor: وفصل بين الجمل للاعتناء بأمر التشنيع والوعيد حيث أشعر أن كل جملة مقصودة على حيالها

ALUSI:96:13/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r25.claim: The passage escalates: first it condemns forbidding prayer without regard to the forbidding person’s supposed status, then condemns it if he claims guidance, then if he actually denies prayer’s truth and turns away.
ALUSI:96:13/r25.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي

ALUSI:96:13/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r28.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r28.claim: One parse makes the first raʾayta visual, needing no second object, and the second and third cognitive, with their conditional clauses and answers filling the second-object position.
ALUSI:96:13/r28.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان

ALUSI:96:13/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r29.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r29.claim: Another parse treats all three as cognitive: the first takes the relative clause as object one, its condition as object two, and the third omits object one while explicitly supplying the threatening answer.
ALUSI:96:13/r29.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول

ALUSI:96:13/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r30.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r30.claim: In that parse, the final clause is unjoined to reinforce the rebuke and signal the condition’s truth; stating its answer makes the threat explicit, while the first conditional’s answer is understood from the second.
ALUSI:96:13/r30.anchor: وفي الإتيان بالجملة الأخيرة من دون العطف ترشيح للكلام المبكت وتنبيه على حقية الشرط

ALUSI:96:13/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r31.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r31.claim: A further parse makes the second and third raʾayta repetitions of the first; both conditionals fill its second-object slot, 96:14 answers the second, and the first answer is omitted by analogy.
ALUSI:96:13/r31.anchor: وقيل أرأيت في الجملتين الثانية والثالثة تكرار للأولى

ALUSI:96:13/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r35.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r35.claim: The prohibitor and worshipper are outside the addressee role in the immediate context; al-Baḥr prefers addressing the Prophet, while another permits addressing the unbelieving prohibitor in a generic scene.
ALUSI:96:13/r35.anchor: ولم يجعلوا فيما ذكر الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا للكافر الناهي

ALUSI:96:13/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r37.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r37.claim: Another proposal shifts the second question’s addressee to the disbeliever and the third’s to the Prophet, like a judge addressing two litigants; its “or” is division equivalent to “and.”
ALUSI:96:13/r37.anchor: فهو عز وجل كالحاكم الذي حضر الخصمان يخاطب هذا مرة والآخر أخرى

ALUSI:96:13/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r40.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r40.claim: A different view says the first clause describes forbidding someone during prayer, not necessarily forbidding prayer itself; since prayer both perfects the worshipper and calls others, the prohibition may target both.
ALUSI:96:13/r40.anchor: وعامة أحوال الصلاة لما انحصرت في تكميل أنفس المصلي بالعبادة وتكميل غيره بالدعوة

ALUSI:96:13/r42.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r42.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:13/r42.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as tyranny born of self-sufficiency, 96:11–12 as rebuke for forfeiting guidance and piety, and 96:13 as rebuke for earning punishment and distance from God; 96:14 is a severe threat.
ALUSI:96:13/r42.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:13/r43.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r43.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:13/r43.claim: For ʿIṣām al-Dīn, the opening question testifies to tyranny: the self-sufficient person goes beyond ingratitude and makes the servant sent to stop it commit ingratitude.
ALUSI:96:13/r43.anchor: عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:13/r46.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r46.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r46.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls ʿIṣām al-Dīn’s overall reading far-fetched and leaves the intent to God after reviewing the preceding analyses.
ALUSI:96:13/r46.anchor: وهو كما ترى فتأمل جميع ما تقدم والله تعالى بمراده أعلم

ALUSI:96:13/r47.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r47.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r47.claim: Although revealed about Abū Jahl, the threat applies to everyone who prohibits prayer; this does not forbid objecting to prayer in usurped places or disliked times, since the objection concerns a concomitant quality, not prayer itself.
ALUSI:96:13/r47.anchor: ثم إن الآية وإن نزلت في أبي جهل عليه اللعنة لكن كل من نهى عن الصلاة ومنع منها فهو شريكه في الوعيد

ALUSI:96:13/r48.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r48.speaker: علي
ALUSI:96:13/r48.claim: ʿAlī, seeing people pray before the Eid prayer, said he had not seen the Prophet do so; asked why he did not forbid them, he feared the threat, or said he preferred to teach what he had seen rather than forbid a worshipper.
ALUSI:96:13/r48.anchor: فروي عن أمير المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه رأى في المصلي أقواماً يصلون قبل صلاة العيد

ALUSI:96:13/r49.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r49.speaker: أبو يوسف
ALUSI:96:13/r49.claim: Abū Yūsuf asked Abū Ḥanīfa whether a worshipper should say “My Lord, forgive me” while rising from bowing; Abū Ḥanīfa prescribed the praise formula and prostration without explicitly forbidding it.
ALUSI:96:13/r49.anchor: فقد روي أن أبا يوسف قال له أيقول المصلي حين يرفع رأسه من الركوع

ALUSI:96:13/r50.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r50.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r50.claim: By analogy, the caution applies to prohibiting other forms of worship; there is no difference between verbal and situational prohibition, including distracting someone from worship, a widespread practice.
ALUSI:96:13/r50.anchor: ويقاس على النهي عن الصلاة النهي عن غيرها من أنواع العبادة ولا فرق بين النهي القالي والنهي الحالي

BAGHAWI:96:9/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:9/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:9/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about Abu Jahl, who forbade the Prophet from praying.
BAGHAWI:96:9/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة

BAGHAWI:96:9/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:9/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI:96:9/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad while praying, his recoil at an unseen trench of fire and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would seize him; the narrator is unsure whether the revelation notice came in this report or elsewhere.
BAGHAWI:96:9/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : " قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم ؟ فقيل : نعم

BAGHAWI:96:9/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:9/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:9/r3.claim: Arayta here expresses amazement to the listener.
BAGHAWI:96:9/r3.anchor: ومعنى { أرأيت } ها هنا تعجيب للمخاطب

BAGHAWI:96:10/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:10/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:10/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about Abu Jahl, who forbade the Prophet from praying.
BAGHAWI:96:10/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة

BAGHAWI:96:10/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:10/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI:96:10/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad while praying, his recoil at an unseen trench of fire and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would seize him; the narrator is unsure whether the revelation notice came in this report or elsewhere.
BAGHAWI:96:10/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : " قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم ؟ فقيل : نعم

BAGHAWI:96:10/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:10/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:10/r3.claim: Arayta here expresses amazement to the listener.
BAGHAWI:96:10/r3.anchor: ومعنى { أرأيت } ها هنا تعجيب للمخاطب

BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.claim: The sentence contrasts the forbidden servant, who is guided and commands piety, with the forbidding man, who denies and turns away; Baghawi calls the contrast astonishing.
BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.anchor: وتقدير نظم الآية : أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى ، والمنهي على الهدى ، آمر بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول عن الإيمان

BAYDAWI:96:9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:9/r1.speaker: أبو جهل
BAYDAWI:96:9/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about Abū Jahl: he threatened to trample Muhammad's neck while prostrating, approached, then retreated, reporting a trench of fire, terror, and wings between them.
BAYDAWI:96:9/r1.anchor: في أبي جهل ، قال : لو رأيت محمدا ساجدا

BIQAI:96:9/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:9/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه
BIQAI:96:9/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra's report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim recounts Abū Jahl approaching Muhammad to smash his head with a rock, then recoiling in terror; versions describe wings, a fiery trench, or a huge camel blocking him.
BIQAI:96:9/r1.anchor: وأصل الحديث في صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

BIQAI:96:9/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:9/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:9/r2.claim: When araʾayta is not visual, it means inform me: know inwardly with a clarity comparable to eyesight.
BIQAI:96:9/r2.anchor: إذا لم يكن بصرياً كان بمعنى أخبر

BIQAI:96:9/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:9/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:9/r3.claim: The verb yanhā depicts the forbidding as renewed and continuous.

IBNASHUR:96:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r1.claim: Kallā rebuts and cancels; because the preceding sentence offers nothing to reject, its opening placement signals that the following statement warrants refutation, like Imruʾ al-Qays's opening negative oath.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r1.anchor: وحرف { كلاّ } ردع وإبطال ،  وليس في الجملة التي قبله ما يحتمل الإبطال والردع ،  فوجود { كلا } في أول الجملة دليل على أن المقصود بالردع

IBNASHUR:96:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNASHUR:96:6/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the prohibition passage and what follows was revealed about Abū Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad's neck, and treats the passage as beginning at verse 9.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r3.anchor: وقال الطبري :  ذكر أن آية { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } وما بعدها نزلت في أبي جهل

IBNASHUR:96:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r4.claim: The accounts are reconciled by taking verses 9 onward as the direct passage about Abū Jahl and verses 6–8 as its preparatory introduction.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r4.anchor: ووجه الجمع بين الروايتين :  أن النازل في أبي جهل بعضه مقصود وهو ما أوله { أرأيت الذي ينهى } الخ

IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.claim: The general statement that humans transgress when they feel self-sufficient introduces the specific account of the prohibitor, encompassing the challenge through Abū Jahl's invitation to his assembly.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.anchor: فموقع قوله :  { إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى } موقع المقدمة لما يرد بعده من قوله :  { أرأيت الذي ينهى

IBNASHUR:96:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:9/r1.claim: The question about the one who prohibits prayer is the intended target of the opening rebuke and follows the general statement about human transgression.
IBNASHUR:96:9/r1.anchor: وجملة :  { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } إلى آخرها هي المقصود من الردع الذي أفاده حرف { كلاّ }

IBNASHUR:96:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:9/r2.claim: The scholars identify the prohibitor as Abū Jahl: he announced in his assembly that he would trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him pray at the Kaʿba, implicitly threatening to stop him; no face-to-face prohibition is reported.
IBNASHUR:96:9/r2.anchor: و{ الذي ينهى } اتفقوا على أنه أريد به أبو جهل إذ قال قولاً يريد به نهي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يصلي في المسجد الحرام

IBNASHUR:96:9/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:9/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:9/r3.claim: Arāʾayta is an expression of astonishment at a state known to have been witnessed; its raʾā is mental knowledge, and its second object is omitted but supplied by the closing question at verse 14.
IBNASHUR:96:9/r3.anchor: تُقال للذي يُعْلَم أنه رأى حالاً عجيبة .  والرؤية علمية ،  أي أعلمت الذي ينهى

IBNASHUR:96:9/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:9/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:9/r4.claim: The interrogative expresses amazement: a remarkable event is framed as a question to confirm news that is hard to believe; this is a transferred rhetorical use, as in the opening question of Sūrat al-Ghāshiyah.
IBNASHUR:96:9/r4.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في التعجيب لأن الحالة العجيبة من شأنها أن يستفهم عن وقوعها استفهام تحقيق وتثبيت لنبئها إذ لا يكاد يصدق به

IBNASHUR:96:9/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:9/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:9/r5.claim: He also allows raʾā to be literal sight, since the verse recounts an event that occurred in the world, with an unspecified addressee.
IBNASHUR:96:9/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الرؤية بصرية لأنها حكاية أمر وقع في الخارج والخطاب في { أرأيت } لغير معين

IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.claim: The pronouns in kadhdhaba and tawallā refer to the prohibitor in verses 9–10; context directs pronouns to their different antecedents, and the object of kadhdhaba is omitted because it is understood as the praying servant.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.anchor: وضمير { كذب وتولى } عائد إلى { الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } [ العلق :  9 ،  10 ]

IBNATIYYA:96:8/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:8/r4.speaker: المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:96:8/r4.claim: The commentators unanimously identify the one who forbids as Abu Jahl and the praying servant as Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA:96:8/r4.anchor: ولم يختلف أحد من المفسرين في أن الناهي : أبو جهل ، وأن العبد المصلي محمد

IBNATIYYA:96:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r1.claim: Arayta is an interrogative challenge and, unlike knowledge-based vision, does not take two objects.
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { أرأيت } توقيف ، وهو فعل لا يتعدى إلى مفعولين على حد الرؤية

IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.anchor: فجاء بها في نسق ، ثم جاء بالوعيد الكافي لجميعها اختصاراً واقتضاباً

IBNKATHIR:96:9/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the passage was revealed about Abū Jahl, who threatened the Prophet for praying at the House.
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، لعنه الله ، توعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:96:9/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r2.claim: God first admonishes the forbidding man in the gentlest manner.
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r2.anchor: فوعظه الله تعالى بالتي هي أحسن أولا

MAWARDI:96:9/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:9/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:9/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about Abu Jahl. Abu Hurayra reports that he vowed by al-Lat and al-ʿUzza to trample Muhammad's neck and soil his face, then approached him in prayer but recoiled; he said a trench of fire, terror, and wings stood between them.
MAWARDI:96:9/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، روى أبو هريرة أن أبا جهل قال : واللات والعزّى لئن رأيت محمداً

MAWARDI:96:9/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:9/r2.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI:96:9/r2.claim: The Prophet said that if Abu Jahl came near, angels would seize him limb by limb; al-Tirmidhi grades this report hasan sahih gharib.
MAWARDI:96:9/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " لو دنا مني لاختطفته الملائكة

MAWARDI:96:9/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:9/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:96:9/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reports the Prophet saying that every nation has a Pharaoh and Abu Jahl is this nation's Pharaoh.
MAWARDI:96:9/r3.anchor: وروى الحسن أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " إنّ لكل أمة فرعون

MAWARDI:96:9/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:9/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:9/r4.claim: The prayer Abu Jahl meant to interrupt was the noon prayer.
MAWARDI:96:9/r4.anchor: وكانت الصلاة التي قصد فيها أبو جهل رسول الله صلاة الظهر

MAWARDI:96:9/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:9/r5.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
MAWARDI:96:9/r5.claim: Jaʿfar b. Muhammad says this may have been Islam's first congregational prayer: Muhammad prayed with ʿAli; Abu Talib passed with Jaʿfar, urged him to support his cousin, and left rejoicing.
MAWARDI:96:9/r5.anchor: وحكى جعفر بن محمد أن أول صلاة جماعة جمعت في الإسلام ، يوشك أن تكون التي أنكرها أبو جهل

MAWARDI:96:9/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:9/r6.speaker: أبو طالب
MAWARDI:96:9/r6.claim: In Jaʿfar's account, Abu Talib's verses call ʿAli and Jaʿfar trustworthy in adversity and vow that he and men of honor will not abandon the Prophet.
MAWARDI:96:9/r6.anchor: إنَّ عليّاً وجعفرا ثقتي *** عند مُلِمِّ الزمان والكُرَبِ

NASAFI:96:14/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:14/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:14/r2.claim: “The one who forbids” and the conditional clause are the two objects of the first “Have you seen?”; its omitted answer is supplied from the second condition, while the repeated question adds emphasis.
NASAFI:96:14/r2.anchor: { الذى ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية مفعولا { أَرَأَيْتَ }

QURTUBI:96:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:9/r1.claim: The one who forbids is Abu Jahl, and the servant he forbids is Muhammad; Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying, prompting these verses in astonishment.
QURTUBI:96:9/r1.anchor: وهو أبو جهل " عبدا " وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم . فإن أبا جهل قال

QURTUBI:96:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:9/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:9/r2.claim: An implied question asks whether the one forbidding prayer is safe from punishment.
QURTUBI:96:9/r2.anchor: وقيل : في الكلام حذف ، والمعنى : أمن هذا الناهي عن الصلاة من العقوبة .

RAZI:96:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r3.claim: Others say the passage about Abū Jahl begins at the verse about the one who forbids a worshipper and continues to the sūra’s end.
RAZI:96:6/r3.anchor: وقيل : نزلت من قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا }

RAZI:96:9/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r1.speaker: أبو جهل
RAZI:96:9/r1.claim: A report says Abū Jahl asked whether Muhammad prostrated in public, vowed to trample his neck if he saw it, then recoiled from the praying Prophet and described a fiery ditch and dreadful terror between them.
RAZI:96:9/r1.anchor: روي عن أبي جهل لعنه الله أنه قال

RAZI:96:9/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:96:9/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Umayya b. Khalaf used to forbid Salmān from praying.
RAZI:96:9/r2.anchor: عن الحسن أن أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة

RAZI:96:9/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r3.claim: The wording points back to the human just mentioned, explaining the identification with Abū Jahl; revelation may have concerned him and then apply generally, though what follows points to a specific man.
RAZI:96:9/r3.anchor: المراد في هذه الآية هو الإنسان المتقدم ذكره

RAZI:96:9/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r4.claim: The question addresses the Prophet in astonishment: he had prayed for Islam to be strengthened through either Abū Jahl or ʿUmar, yet how could a man who forbids prayer strengthen it?
RAZI:96:9/r4.anchor: اللهم أعز الإسلام إما بأبي جهل بن هشام أو بعمر

RAZI:96:9/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r5.claim: The question mocks Abū al-Ḥakam’s title: how can a man who prevents service to God and prostrates to idols rightly be called wise?

RAZI:96:9/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r6.claim: The question exposes the folly of a mere creature who issues commands and expects obedience while forbidding service to the true Creator and Lord.

RAZI:96:9/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r7.claim: The indefinite servant signals complete, sincere servitude, so forbidding the most devoted creature from worship is sheer ignorance.
RAZI:96:9/r7.anchor: التنكير في عبدا يدل على كونه كاملا في العبودية

RAZI:96:9/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r8.claim: An account has a Jewish eloquent man ask ʿUmar about the Prophet’s character; ʿAlī replies that if the man cannot describe worldly goods, which God calls little, he cannot describe the Prophet’s character, which God calls great.
RAZI:96:9/r8.anchor: يهوديا من فصحاء اليهود جاء إلى عمر في أيام خلافته

RAZI:96:9/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r9.claim: The indefinite wording also portrays this as the forbidding man’s habitual conduct toward anyone he sees.
RAZI:96:9/r9.anchor: هذا دأبه وعادته فينهى كل من يرى

RAZI:96:9/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r10.claim: The verse warns anyone who forbids prayer; ʿAlī, seeing people pray before the Eid prayer, declined to stop them because he feared falling under its warning.
RAZI:96:9/r10.anchor: روي عن علي عليه السلام أنه رأى في المصلى أقواما

RAZI:96:9/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI:96:9/r11.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa follows the same tact: when Abū Yūsuf asked whether a worshipper should say a forgiveness prayer after bowing, he prescribed the established praise and prostration without explicitly forbidding it.
RAZI:96:9/r11.anchor: أخذ أبو حنيفة منه هذا الأدب الجميل

RAZI:96:9/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r12.claim: The worshipper is one servant among many: if Muhammad did not prostrate, innumerable proximate angels would still remain constantly in prayer and praise.
RAZI:96:9/r12.anchor: ولي من الملائكة المقربين مالا يحصيهم إلا أنا

RAZI:96:9/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:9/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:96:9/r13.claim: Though indefinite, servant is identified as the Prophet and thus magnifies his station; Rāzī compares this to Quranic references where a servant is understood without prior mention.
RAZI:96:9/r13.anchor: نظيره الكناية في سورة القدر حملت على القرآن
